All five orders are live and working (status `new`, resting as day limit orders — they're marketable-ish debit limits, so they should fill during the session; if any don't fill I'd revisit before end of day, but no further action is needed right now).

## Summary — 2026-08-28 earnings calendar scan

**Starting state:** Flat account, $100,000 equity, no open positions or orders — clean slate, so this whole batch is net-new.

**Universe reviewed:** All 8 Tier-A candidates from today's scan (DELL, PANW, MDB, AVGO, SNOW, CIEN, LULU, ZS), all flagged `candidate: true` with front/back ATM ratios from 1.44–1.81. No Tier B names were in this list, so nothing to flag/skip there.

**Liquidity screen:** Pulled live option chains for the exact front (9/4) and back (10/2) ATM strikes the scan specified, and computed bid/ask spread as a % of mid on each leg:

| Ticker | Front spread % | Back spread % | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|
| DELL | 2.0% | 8.2% | ✅ trade |
| AVGO | 7.5% | 10.6% | ✅ trade |
| ZS | 11.2% | 7.2% | ✅ trade |
| SNOW | 11.2% | 10.4% | ✅ trade |
| LULU | 11.7% | 9.6% | ✅ trade |
| PANW | 9.6% | 14.0% | ❌ skip — back leg too wide |
| MDB | 16.9% | 18.6% | ❌ skip — both legs thin |
| CIEN | 22.2% | 15.8% | ❌ skip — front leg extremely wide |

PANW, MDB, and CIEN all showed real quotes but with spreads wide enough (14–22% of mid) that a fill would eat a meaningful chunk of the edge before the trade even starts working — skipped per the liquidity rule rather than forced.

**Positions opened** (sell front ATM call / buy back ATM call, same strike, net debit, day limit at approx mid):

| Ticker | Strike | Front/Back | Qty | Net debit/spread | Total debit | % of equity |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| DELL | 470 | 9/4 · 10/2 | 1 | $15.95 | $1,595 | 1.6% |
| AVGO | 367.5/365 | 9/4 · 10/2 | 3 | $7.86 | $2,358 | 2.4% |
| ZS | 180 | 9/4 · 10/2 | 8 | $3.53 | $2,824 | 2.8% |
| SNOW | 340 | 9/4 · 10/2 | 5 | $5.28 | $2,640 | 2.6% |
| LULU | 116 | 9/4 · 10/2 | 14 | $2.11 | $2,954 | 3.0% |

Sizing logic: target 2.5–3% of equity per debit, capped hard at 3% (never crossed). Each ticker's per-contract debit is fixed by its option price, so I took the largest integer contract count that stayed ≤3%. ZS, SNOW, and LULU landed cleanly in the 2.5–3% band. AVGO landed just under band (2.4%) because the next contract up would have pushed to 3.14%, breaching the cap. DELL is the outlier — its per-contract debit (~$1,595) is high enough relative to the 3% ceiling that even 1 contract only uses 1.6% of equity; 2 contracts would have been 3.2%, over the cap, so 1 contract was the compliant choice even though it undersizes relative to the target band. This is a granularity artifact of high-priced options, not a discretionary under-sizing.

**Position count:** 5 new calendars, well within the 6–8 cap, no duplicates with existing positions (there were none).

**Not acted on:** PANW, MDB, CIEN — liquidity too thin on the exact contracts needed, explained above. No Tier B names present today to flag.

**Rolling:** N/A today — no pre-existing positions to roll.

This is a first-cut, rules-based execution — sizing and liquidity cutoffs were mechanical, not conviction-driven, consistent with treating this as an unvalidated strategy.
